## Summary

Define Cardinality Notation

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
p{:occurrence}: [value format]{:value count};

p.*[immediate name format]{:immediate name count};

p.**[recursive name format]{:recursive name count};

p.*[name format]{:name count}: [value format]{:value count}
```

### Prose Claim


Cardinality annotations state allowed counts; they do not count a value merely
because a dependent Property exists. `{:n}` allows exactly n, `{:n+}` at
least n, and `{:n..m}` the inclusive range for its qualified selection. Bounds
are non-negative integers with n not greater than m. `{=n}` is a count
condition/test, `{>n}` is a count condition/test that compares the actual count
with n using the existing numeric `>`, and `{==n}` a required or derived count
conclusion; none is an allowed bound. A direct parent-value count excludes
nested child keys and every descendant value, including every value held by
nested children.

Property occurrence, value and dependent-name counts are separate:


`p{:0}` forbids authored occurrences of p; it does not forbid independently
declared children. `p.*[]{:0}` states that p has no declared immediate
dependents after local and inherited declaration resolution. The value count
to the right of `[value format]` is per selected existing Property occurrence;
the name count is the number of selected dependent Property names. A recursive
name count aggregates selected distinct descendant Property identities under p
within each selected bearer; it does not count direct values or another
bearer's descendants.

`Source {:forward}((RELATION)){:reverse} Target` has independent directional
counts. The first constrains outgoing Relation instances per selected Source;
the second constrains reverse links per selected Target. Reversing the written
Relation swaps the slots. Neither count is a Property value count, a distinct
target count, or Relation arity. An omitted annotation is unspecified.

## Summary

Bind instance variables

## Claim

### Prose Claim


- `Kind//` selects existing instances of Kind and its narrower kinds.
- `Kind//{:n}` applies the existing cardinality to the selected logical instances within the Project context. Resolve the complete selection and count each instance once across repeated references or Carrier representations. An unresolved population is an error.
- `Kind//$x` ranges over the selected instances. Each non-aggregate per-binding constraint must hold for every matching binding. Repeated `$x` references in one Claim block identify the same instance within each binding; an enclosing aggregate retains its selected population.
- `in` and `not in` test an instance's identity against a selected instance set. `=` and `!=` compare bound instance references by identity; they do not test kind membership or broadcast a scalar comparison over a set.
- `Kind//$x.p` selects and binds an instance and reads its Property `p`. `$x.p` reads that same bound instance's Property.
- In an IF condition, `Kind//$c ((R)) Kind//$p` tests a link that already exists, including a legitimately derived inverse. It is not an endpoint signature and does not create a link.
- Evaluate the condition for candidate bindings. Its THEN conclusion applies only to bindings for which that link exists; it does not require links between every candidate pair.
- Endpoint counts aggregate matching links per endpoint; they do not require a link between every pair of bindings.
- Binding selects existing instances. It does not create an instance named `$x` or assign a value imperatively. A bare qualified address refers to its declared target.

In one CFEL Formal Claim fence, the full-line comments `# model` and `# instances` distinguish MODEL constraints from instance constraints. When both are present, write `# model` first. These comments are not operators, Properties, or values. Named MODEL addresses such as `Relation//NAME` and `Operator//NAME` retain their declared identity; a Relation descriptor variable in the MODEL group does not make it a runtime instance constraint.

In the MODEL group, `IF $x in (selection) THEN (conclusion)` binds an unbound `$x` over the selected MODEL entities. If `$x` is already bound, the membership test filters that same binding. References to `$x` throughout the parenthesized conclusion use the same binding; the conclusion may contain nested conditions and semicolon-separated statements. This does not create a MODEL entity or introduce a FOR operator.

`KindSelection//$x` binds existing members of the selected logical instance population. The receiver may be a named Kind or a union Kind selection: `(in (Action, Workflow))//$selected` keeps the Action-or-Workflow population and binds its matching members. An existing filter follows the explicit binder without changing its matching population, as in `Event Record//$event_record(.object_output{=1}, .object_output.id = $projection.ID)`. In an aggregate such as `MAX(Event Record//$event_record(.object_output{=1}).happened_at)`, the argument remains the complete filtered population; inserting the binder does not turn the aggregate into one calculation per selected row.

`Kind//$x{:n}` constrains the count of the entire selected logical population in its Project context, not a count of one already-bound row. The existing `Kind//{:n}` population rule remains readable for historical sources. Neither a binder nor a named reference creates an instance, Property, Relation fact or imperative assignment. Binding alone does not grant an inverse permission or change endpoint counts.

Kind//$x
```

This binds one existing selected instance.

## Summary

Use distinct graph notation for Node relations

## Claim

### Prose Claim

In Subject addresses and Formal Claims, `X/Y` selects a narrower declared kind and `X//Name` an instance of a declared kind. A Property cannot narrow or instantiate. `X.p` addresses a Property borne by X; an unchanged inherited Property is resolved to its existing declaration rather than redeclared or given another bearer. In Subject addresses, `X/(.p := V)` admits V as a Property value and selects the whole Primary Node X where p equals V. The case does not exclude other allowed values from X.p. `(Node, Node.**)` selects Node and its recursive dependent Properties; it is not a narrowing assertion. Shared Node rules are declared once and inherited by applicable narrower Nodes.

`Part +> Whole` and `Whole <+ Part` are opposite written views of one composition fact, not narrowing. `X >| Axis` and `Axis |< X` are opposite views of one classification fact. `:` marks an allowed value. `=` tests a condition; `==` sets a value. Parentheses group expressions; `in (a, b)` expresses membership. A bare Entity name refers to the existing target without copying or reparenting it.

For `Source {:left}((NAME)){:right} Target`, each optional bound constrains Relation instances at its written endpoint. Reversing the written view swaps the bounds. A Node-specific Claim addresses its active Node and its own bound; a Relation Declaration can state both intrinsic endpoint bounds. The opposite view requires its own applicable permission; a reverse written view does not grant permission. `{:n}` states an allowed cardinality. The same notation can constrain Properties, instances and Relations. Repeated references in a rule, including its conditions and conclusions, bind the same selected member. An omitted cardinality annotation leaves that cardinality undefined; it is not an implicit zero or permission.

`(Node, Node.**)` selects model Entities in the Node branch; it does not limit other declared Entities. `(Node//, (Node//).**)` is the instance-layer selector. `Node//` selects Node instances including instances of narrower kinds. `(Node//).**` selects recursive Property occurrences of a Node instance; it does not independently instantiate a Property kind. The two layers have separate permissions. Repeated instance matches count once by identity.

Subjects remain addresses and do not contain complete Formal Claims. In Subjects, `:=` combines allowed value and condition, including `Atom.Header.Status := Draft` and `Atom/(.Header.Role := Method)`; it does not write an instance value. Formal Claims retain separate `:` and `=` meanings. The withdrawn `..` form is not adopted; `::` has no assigned meaning here.

## Dependent selection

- `x.*`: immediate dependents.
- `x.**`: all dependents recursively.

A Property's full path determines its identity. Sibling names must be unique.

## Expression lists

Separate complete expressions with `;`. A line break is layout. Boolean groups remain one expression.

## RMED

RMED names these Roles:

- Requirement.
- Method.
- Evaluation.
- Delivery.

## Formal content

A Formal Claim is a declared child of an ordinary RMED Claim and contains formal content in a fenced block labelled CFEL. Formal content in an ordinary RMED Claim belongs in Formal Claim. Prose Claim contains ordinary Markdown. A heading in a Markdown value does not declare a Property by itself. Unknown headings, including `##` headings, within Prose Claim remain part of that value and do not terminate it.

## Inherited Node selection

- `Node.**` selects recursive dependent Properties.
- `(Node//).**` selects their occurrences on a Node instance.
- Node rules are inherited by applicable narrower Nodes.
- Commas combine selectors within one expression.
- Semicolons separate expressions.

## Claim

### Prose Claim


- `p{:occurrence}` constrains occurrences of the named Property.
- `p{:occurrence}: [value format]{:value count}` constrains its direct values.
- `p.*[name format]{:child count}` constrains immediate dependent names.

  across every descendant depth.
- `p.*[name format]{:child count}: [value format]{:value count}` also
  constrains each selected immediate dependent Property's direct values.
- The name count and value count are different counts. Separate complete
  expressions use `;`.

- `p.*.*` selects Properties exactly two levels below p.
- `p.*.**` selects Properties two or more levels below p.

distinct descendant Property identities below p within each selected bearer.

## Summary

Define CFEL

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
p{:occurrence}: [value format]{:value count};

p.*[name format]{:immediate name count};

p.**[name format]{:recursive name count};

p.*[name format]{:immediate name count}: [value format]{:value count}
```

### Prose Claim

CFEL (CAPRMEDIO Formal Expression Language) is the formal notation for
Subject addresses and fenced Formal Claims. CFEL is a model component beside
Graph and Carrier: Graph contains Nodes and Relations; CFEL addresses and
constrains them. CFEL syntax neither creates a Node, Relation, Property,
Carrier fact, Workflow step, nor evaluator result.

An `IF` membership condition can bind an unbound variable to each matching member of its declared selection; a variable already bound in the surrounding scope is tested against membership without rebinding. A parenthesized multi-line `THEN` body uses the same binding in each complete expression. This does not introduce a `FOR` primitive.

In a Formal Claim, `#model` and `#instances` are ordering comments for the model and instance expressions that follow; they do not assert graph facts. A `$variable` explicitly binds an anonymous selected Entity or instance; repeated occurrences in its scope select the same identity. A typed selector supplies its universe; use model variables where model entities are intended. These bindings introduce no new binding operator.

CFEL uses these graph-address forms:

- `X/Y` selects a narrower Primary Node; `X//Name` selects an existing
  instance of a Primary Node.
- `X.p` addresses Property p borne by X. In a Subject only,
  `X/(.p := V)` combines an admitted Property value with selection of X;
  `:=` is not a Formal-Claim value assignment.
- `Part +> Whole` and `Whole <+ Part` are opposite written views of one
  containment fact. `X >| Axis` and `Axis |< X` are opposite written views
  of one classification fact. A bare qualified address references its declared entity or instance. No `@` reference operator is required; `@N` identity/version tags retain their separate meaning.
- Parentheses group one expression. `;` separates complete expressions;
  a line break has no conjunction or disjunction meaning.

In Formal Claims, `X: Y` admits Y as an allowed value of X regardless of X's
kind or preceding path; it is not assignment. `=` and `!=` test conditions,
and `==` states a required or derived conclusion. `in` and `not in` are the
admitted membership tests. Numeric comparison and addition use the separately
defined `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=` and `+`; they are distinct from Relation
operators. Property occurrence, direct-value, immediate-name
and recursive-name counts are distinct:

`{:n}`, `{:n+}` and `{:n..m}` state allowed cardinality bounds on their
qualified selection; `{=n}` tests a count condition, `{>n}` tests whether the
actual count is greater than n using the existing numeric `>`, and `{==n}`
concludes a required or derived count. These test/conclusion forms are not
allowed bounds. A Relation has independent outgoing and
reverse cardinalities: `Source {:forward}((RELATION)){:reverse} Target`.
Omitted annotations are unspecified, not zero. `[format]` applies to direct
values; a name selector is not a value selector. A `p.**` count aggregates
selected distinct descendant Property identities below p within each selected
bearer, independently of direct values and other bearers.

The following named constructs are admitted only with the semantics in their
own CFEL Rules: `IF`/`THEN`, `UNIQUE`, `DETERMINES`, `COUNT`, `MAX`,
`LOOKUP`, `FENCED_LABELS`, and `?=`. `>>` is delivery notation with the
semantics of the delivery Rule; `!(selectors)` excludes branches from a
delivery selection. `Kind//$x` binds an existing selected instance and `$x.p`
reads its Property. Each non-graph CFEL operator has its own Declaration;
an operator is not a binary Node Relation. A Requirement/Declaration describes
a canonical or derived Relation direction; it does not authorize a second
stored inverse fact.

The reusable metadata family `Operator//Name == "notation literal"` binds a
declared operator descriptor to its token or bounded construct spelling. Its
quoted right side is metadata, not an executed CFEL expression, value assignment,
state creation, or a new model entity.

A direct Relation Declaration owns shared meaning and endpoints. A derived inverse Declaration retains the reverse HAS_INVERSE binding and its own alias, when present. A qualified or other non-inverse derived view retains its source, endpoint transformation and qualification; derivation alone does not imply unconditional endpoint reversal. `alias(Relation//NAME) == "token"` binds exact Relation names to lexical notation. `Relation//DIRECT <--> Relation//DERIVED` binds distinct inverse Relations in the direct Declaration. It never equates their identities. These metadata forms do not create literal-to-Node graph links.

A graph Relation connects declared model entities or declared instances,
including Carrier and CFEL; it is not limited to `Node/**`. A literal remains a
Property or allowed value, not a graph endpoint. A non-graph CFEL operator is
not itself a graph Relation, but its declared operator descriptor is a model
entity that may be a graph endpoint; an operator glyph or literal operand does
not create another model entity. Each direct Relation Declaration supplies shared meaning and a
formal Host/Target signature with typed selectors whose universe is known, or
with declared variables bound to that universe. Within a Relation Declaration
Formal Claim only, `$host ((RELATION)) $target` is the reusable generic
signature: its untyped variables range over that declared entity-or-instance
universe and exclude literals. It declares neither a Relation fact nor instance
data. Known endpoint kinds remain typed selectors. This generic Relation signature binding applies within Relation Declarations; typed bindings can also select model entities where their universe is declared.

Concrete directional alternatives describe the same canonical Relation fact:
`Step ((IS_CONTAINED_BY)) Workflow` and
`Workflow <((IS_CONTAINED_BY)) Step`. The bare forward form
`Step ((IS_CONTAINED_BY)) Workflow` remains valid. In reverse writing,
normalization swaps canonical Source/Target and the two written endpoint count
slots. This syntax does not grant an inverse Relation permission. The Relation Declaration states the Host, Target and applicable counterpart direction. `HAS_INVERSE` applies to inverse Relations; a qualified non-inverse derived view retains its source, transformation and qualification.

In RMED Claims, all formal content is a fenced block labelled `CFEL`. CFEL
body syntax and Markdown-fence-label parsing are separate concerns. This Definition
describes the admitted language contract; it does not claim a complete parser
or evaluator. An unimplemented construct remains an adoption and conformance
gap, not evidence that the construct has different semantics.

This Definition does not convert a Format, Bool value, or any other value
into an instance selected by `//`. Such an instance selection requires the
existing source binding that declares it. No value-format-to-instance rewrite
is implied by the CFEL overview.

`Relation//IS_DECLARED_BY` is the qualified derived view of a GOVERNS fact whose source is a Requirement/Form Declaration; it reverses that selected fact while retaining the qualification. It is not a general inverse of GOVERNS or a permission for every Relation.
